title: A familiar Iranian hacking group has found a new way to cause chaos
gist: French intelligence attributes an October cyberattack that raised temperatures in refrigeration systems at hundreds of French supermarkets, destroying millions of euros of food, to IRGC hacking unit Shahid Kaveh (CyberAv3ngers) — an escalation of Iranian targeting into European infrastructure amid the US-Israel campaign against Iran. Experts flag possible Russian collaboration and note the low-sophistication, Modbus-based attack burned a capability to send a message.

insights.claim: In October, hackers raised temperatures in refrigeration systems at hundreds of supermarkets across France, destroying millions of euros of food — an unprecedented scale for attacks on commercial fridges and freezers.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Connected retail/cold-chain equipment is now a demonstrated attack surface — a driver for OT security spending by grocers.
insights.locator: One night in October, hackers staged

insights.claim: Similar refrigeration attacks were staged against supermarkets in 10 other European countries this month, though no group has yet been blamed.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Campaign is spreading across Europe; insurers and retailers face correlated cyber-physical losses.
insights.locator: Similar attacks were staged this month

insights.claim: French intelligence says Shahid Kaveh used a Chinese-made scanning tool to find Internet-connected refrigeration units and conducted reconnaissance using the Modbus industrial control protocol, a technique used since at least April.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Internet-exposed Modbus devices are the weak link — benefits OT/ICS security vendors and network segmentation.
insights.locator: French intelligence agencies have said the group used

insights.claim: French intelligence found Farsi traces and other clues tying the supermarket hack to Shahid Kaveh, an elite hacking unit under the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps' Cyber Electronic Command, also known as CyberAv3ngers.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: State attribution raises the odds of sanctions and diplomatic escalation between Europe and Iran.
insights.locator: But French intelligence agencies found traces of Farsi

insights.claim: CyberAv3ngers hacked Israeli-made industrial control devices in water, manufacturing and transportation systems across several US states in 2023 and 2024, causing minimal disruption but leaving anti-Israel messages.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Track record shows the group's focus on critical infrastructure using Israeli-made equipment.
insights.quote: Every equipment ‘made in Israel’ is CyberAv3ngers legal target.
insights.locator: The group, which often goes by the online persona

insights.claim: France is seeking international arrest warrants for Hamid Reza Lashgarian, believed to head the IRGC Cyber Electronic Command, and Shahid Kaveh leaders Mahdi Lashgarian and Reza Salarvand, while Iran denies involvement.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Formal legal action signals European willingness to escalate against Iranian cyber operations.
insights.locator: Iran has denied any role in the freezer hacks

insights.claim: Experts say the October supermarket hacks mark an escalation in Iran's cyber warfare strategy and a new willingness to hit European infrastructure, as Iran increasingly views all Nato countries as legitimate targets.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: European critical infrastructure faces rising Iranian cyber risk even for countries not in the US-Israel campaign.
insights.quote: This is about sowing panic in Europe and increasing that global pain threshold.
insights.locator: While France and other European countries have largely stayed out

insights.claim: Ellie Geranmayeh of the European Council on Foreign Relations says Iran has clearly messaged that the global economy will be disrupted as a consequence of being shut out from the world.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Expect more economically targeted cyber disruption tied to Iran's isolation.
insights.quote: Iran has very clearly messaged that the global economy will be disrupted as a consequence of it being shut out from the world,

insights.claim: Chatham House's Sanam Vakil says Iran's cyber capabilities are underestimated, built by young engineers and lessons learned from the 2009 Stuxnet attack on its nuclear program.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Underestimation of Iranian cyber capacity implies under-priced cyber risk in Western infrastructure.
insights.quote: Iran is a country of engineers, and people continue to underestimate its capabilities,
insights.locator: Iran is a country of engineers

insights.claim: Former FBI deputy cyber director Cynthia Kaiser says the European refrigeration attacks look more consistent with Russian-type targeting and that a third state may have contracted Shahid Kaveh.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Possible Russia-Iran cyber collaboration would widen the threat set against European infrastructure.
insights.quote: Even if Iranians were behind the keyboard, these attacks really appear more consistent with Russian-type targeting,
insights.locator: Kaiser said it was also possible

insights.claim: Sanam Vakil says the strength of Russia-Iran ties is often under-appreciated by Western officials and has grown through the Ukraine war and Iran's conflict with the US and Israel.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Deeper Russia-Iran alignment raises coordinated hybrid-warfare risk in Europe.
insights.quote: Their ties have grown through the context of these wars,
insights.locator: Vakil at Chatham House acknowledged Russian involvement

insights.claim: Check Point's Gil Messing says the supermarket hack was unsophisticated but required senior IRGC authorization because exploited vulnerabilities are quickly patched, so using the capability burns it.
insights.speaker: Financial Times
insights.so_what: Use of a 'burnable' cyber weapon signals deliberate strategic messaging rather than opportunistic crime.
insights.quote: This is not a very sophisticated attack, but it sends a very strong message.
insights.locator: Cyber weapons have a limited shelf life
